dedupe_keys.name: global infrastructure resilience report 2025 capturing the resilience dividend cdri

description: The Global Infrastructure Resilience Report 2025 makes the economic case for infrastructure resilience, estimating global disaster-related losses above US$732 billion a year and indirect economic impacts averaging 7.4 times direct damage to infrastructure. The Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure produced it, using its Global Infrastructure Risk Model and Resilience Index (GIRI) together with the Green Economy Model to show that reconstruction within ten years can halve GDP losses. It sets out priorities for local risk assessment, layered financing through bonds, insurance and contingency funds, governance reform, technologies such as digital twins and drones, and nature-based solutions, with case studies. Coverage is global, with emphasis on Africa and small island developing states and on renewable energy and irrigation. Format and access: a report downloadable from CDRI's site. Licence: not stated on the page read; free. Caveats: figures are model-based and aggregated, and the underlying scenario data are on the GIRI platform, not in the report. It informs resilience and adaptation investment cases and supplies loss ratios for economic impact modelling. Related catalogue records are the GIRI data platform and the UNDRR and CDRI country applications.
